title: kv-cache: adaptive eviction + spillover heuristics v32 (fragmentation-aware compaction and host-paging policy)
author: Ava Singh
release_notes: Improved KV cache memory management: fragmentation-aware compaction, host spillover priority, and background defragmentation scheduler. Reduces OOMs and tail latency for high-concurrency long-context workloads.
description: Motivation: Production workloads with long-context, diverse sequence lengths, and high concurrency revealed two recurring issues: 1) KV cache fragmentation leading to unusable free space and increased allocations, 2) suboptimal spillover/paging decisions that evict hot keys or cause repeated roundtrips to host memory, increasing tail latency. This PR implements a set of coordinated changes to improve memory utilization and eviction behavior without regressing latency or throughput. Summary of changes: - Fragmentation-aware compaction: add a lightweight compaction pass that runs on allocated arenas when fragmentation crosses a threshold. Compaction is conservative: it merges adjacent free spans and coalesces low-utilization segments instead of full copy compaction, reducing CPU and memcpy overhead. - Adaptive spillover priority buckets: introduce two spillover tiers (cold, warm) determined by access recency + token frequency heuristics. Cold entries are eligible for immediate host paging; warm entries are considered for delayed spillover and prioritized for defragmentation/compaction first. - Background defragmentation scheduler: a rate-limited background worker that opportunistically defragments memory during low-util windows. Scheduler integrates with the serving runtime SLOs and pauses when token latency budgets approach SLO. - Eviction scoring refactor: replace monolithic LRU score with composite scoring (recency, token-frequency, allocation-fragmentation-impact). This reduces evicting high-value entries that are cheaply compressible. - Continuous batching compatibility: ensure KV lifecycle hooks are safe under continuous batching (no blocking critical path operations; compaction happens off the fast-path with epoch-based reclamation). - Metrics and observability: new metrics (kv_compaction_runs_total, kv_fragmentation_ratio, kv_spillover_evicted_cold, kv_spillover_evicted_warm, kv_defrag_worker_latency_ms) and dashboard updates. - Tests & canary: added microbenchmarks and end-to-end canary configs to validate memory usage and tail latency under mixed workload patterns. Checklist: - [x] Implement fragmentation-aware compaction algorithm - [x] Add spillover tiering and scoring changes - [x] Background defrag scheduler with SLO-aware backoff - [x] Add metrics and dashboard notes - [x] Unit tests for scoring/compaction - [x] Integration tests with continuous batching harness - [x] Canary run on perf-lab (passed) Commits (high-level): - 3c1a9f2: add fragmentation tracking and arena metadata - 7b4e6a1: implement compaction pass and unit tests - 8f02d3e: introduce spillover tiers + scoring refactor - b4f9c12: background defrag scheduler + SLO integration hooks - d2a3b7f: add metrics, dashboards and tests for continuous batching safety - e9f1a4b: canary and perf tweaks, doc comments Context and design notes: - Fragmentation tracking: each arena tracks free-span histogram and avg external fragmentation ratio. Thresholds are conservative (e.g. >18% fragmentation triggers compaction attempt). - Compaction strategy: prefer in-place coalescing and small-range copying (<64KB) to limit memcpy cost. Larger compactions are split and scheduled by background worker. - Spillover policy: entries classified by a lightweight hotness score (recent_access_weight + token_count_weight). Cold candidates are paged to host memory; warm candidates are considered for compaction first. This reduces double-migrations for entries that are likely to be accessed soon. - Scheduler SLO-awareness: the defrag worker queries the runtime token latency budget before starting a pass and backs off exponentially if budget is tight. Backpressure hooks expose a runtime_hint to avoid impacting fast-path token servicing. Review highlights: - Marco: requested clearer bounds on compaction CPU usage and a throttling mechanism — added token-budget backoff and per-worker cpu_cooldown_ms. - Priya: asked for deterministic behavior in unit tests; added synthetic allocator to simulate fragmentation patterns. - Ethan: requested metrics for spillover cold/warm evictions — added kv_spillover_evicted_{cold,warm}. CI and validation: - CI: linux unit tests, allocation fuzzing, style checks — all green. - Perf canary: deployed to perf-canary on a mix of 1k concurrent streams with 64k average context; observed 18% reduction in peak GPU memory pressure and 9% tail latency improvement (p95->p95.9) at same throughput. - Reruns: one flaky allocator test was flakey on first run (fuzz harness updated to stabilize); fixed and CI passed. Files changed (high level): - runtime/kv/arena_allocator.{cc,h} - runtime/kv/compactor.{cc,h} - runtime/kv/spillover_policy.{cc,h} - runtime/kv/defrag_scheduler.{cc,h} - runtime/kv/metrics_registry.{cc} - tests/kv/compaction_tests.cc - tests/kv/spillover_policy_tests.cc - docs/observability/kv_metrics.md Implementation notes: - Kept fast-path allocations lock-free where possible; compaction and spillover use epoch-based handoff to avoid stalls. - Added sparse-locking for arena metadata to avoid global contention under high concurrency. - Prefer small-step compactions to avoid long pauses; large compactions are chunked and yield to runtime. Rollout plan: - Canary in perf-canary for 48 hours (completed), then gradual ramp on staging clusters for 24h, then opt-in customer rollouts with feature flag. - Monitoring: alert on kv_compaction_runs_total spike and kv_defrag_worker_latency_ms exceeding 200ms. Related PRs: series of prior eviction/refactor PRs (see linked PRs in repo).

review_comments: Marco Rivera: Please ensure compaction CPU is throttled; we saw a spike in previous experiments.
Ava Singh: Added cpu_cooldown_ms and token-budget backoff; compaction is rate-limited by default (10ms per arena cycle).
Priya Patel: Unit tests were flaky under allocator fuzzing — can you make tests deterministic?
Ava Singh: Added synthetic allocator and reproducible seeds for tests; CI green after update.
Ethan Cole: Can we get metrics that separate cold vs warm spillovers?
Ava Singh: Added kv_spillover_evicted_cold and kv_spillover_evicted_warm; updated dashboards.
ci_summary: All CI checks passed after two runs. Initial flaky test fixed. Perf canary succeeded with reduced memory pressure and tail latency improvements.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on compaction invariants and epoch handoff correctness. Pay attention to scheduler SLO integration and any potential fast-path regressions. Benchmarks and unit tests included.
canary_results: perf-canary: 48h run, ~18% reduction in peak GPU memory, ~9% improvement in tail latency p95.9 at 1k concurrent streams. No increase in error rate.
additional_context: This PR continues iterative series to improve KV memory management (see prior PRs in this directory). It is conservative in default thresholds; operators can tune compaction/spillover via runtime flags.
changelog_entry: runtime(kv): fragmentation-aware compaction and adaptive spillover priority to reduce memory pressure and tail latency
